issue.title: ace.snippet_config_path accepts a destination sase never loads back, so those snippets silently vanish on restart
issue.description:
Found by the sase-j3 land agent while verifying epic sase-j3 (snippet target mode) on master d4b913bb9. Not a plan violation: sase-j3.1 implemented resolve_snippet_save_target() exactly as the approved plan specified. The gap is that the specified rules never check whether sase will read the file back.

WHAT HAPPENS: src/sase/xprompt/snippet_targets.py::resolve_snippet_save_target accepts any configured path whose suffix is .yml/.yaml and whose _writability_reason() is None. But sase's config loader only merges three sources: ~/.config/sase/sase.yml, the ~/.config/sase/sase_*.yml overlays discovered by src/sase/config/loading.py::get_overlay_paths (glob 'sase_*.yml'), and the project sase/sase.yml. src/sase/xprompt/snippet_targets.py::load_snippet_config_locations enumerates exactly that set, so any configured destination outside it is writable but never loaded.

REPRODUCTION (by inspection; not yet run end-to-end): set ace.snippet_config_path to 'snippets.yml'. Rule 2 resolves it to ~/.config/sase/snippets.yml. The parent is writable and the suffix is fine, so it is accepted with source='configured' and fallback_reason=None. gt writes the ace.snippets entry there and _publish_saved_snippet() makes the trigger expand immediately, so the loop looks correct for the rest of the session. On the next ACE start the file is not an overlay ('snippets.yml' does not match 'sase_*.yml') and is not merged, so the snippet is gone with no diagnostic. Any absolute path outside ~/.config/sase/ and the project config has the same shape. Note the near-miss: the docs/configuration.md example uses 'sase_snippets.yml', which does load; dropping the 'sase_' prefix silently does not.

WHY IT NEEDS A DECISION RATHER THAN A DRIVE-BY FIX -- there are two defensible remediations:
  (a) Reject a non-loadable destination in resolve_snippet_save_target and fall back to the default with a fallback_reason. The plumbing already exists: the trigger-name panel renders fallback_reason precisely so a user learns why their preference was not honored. Cheapest and consistent with rule 4.
  (b) Teach the config loader to also read the configured snippet file, honoring the user's choice end-to-end. Larger, but it is what a user setting the field probably expects.
Whichever is chosen, docs/configuration.md's ace.snippet_config_path section needs to state the constraint explicitly.

CARE REQUIRED: sase-j3.8 (commit d4b913bb9) deliberately made UnifiedXPromptSaveModal include a resolved snippet target that is outside the discovered locations. Option (a) narrows what the resolver can return, so re-check that work and its tests in tests/ace/tui/modals/test_unified_xprompt_save_modal.py and tests/ace/tui/actions/test_prompt_save_xprompt_targets.py rather than assuming it becomes dead code.

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-j3 — the epic that added ace.snippet_config_path and resolve_snippet_save_target(); its plan (plans:202608/snippet_target_mode.md, phase 'target') specifies the six resolution rules this task proposes to extend, and its phase bead sase-j3.1 carries the implementation notes.

payload.close_reason: Backlog cut to seven (owner-requested, 2026-08-12): needs an owner design decision, and the trigger is a misconfiguration rather than a default path. The analysis is sound -- resolve_snippet_save_target accepts any writable .yml/.yaml destination, while the config loader only merges ~/.config/sase/sase.yml, the ~/.config/sase/sase_*.yml overlays, and the project sase/sase.yml -- so a configured ace.snippet_config_path outside that set is written and never read back. But it fires only when someone sets that field to a non-loadable path (the docs example, sase_snippets.yml, loads correctly), it was never reproduced end to end, and the bead itself says the two remediations are a judgment call the owner should make, not something to hand an agent. My read if you want a default: option (a) -- reject the non-loadable destination in resolve_snippet_save_target and fall back with a fallback_reason, since the trigger-name panel already renders that field for exactly this purpose -- plus one sentence in docs/configuration.md stating the constraint. Re-file with that decision attached, or with a +1 if a real snippet loss is observed.
